_doc: Generated-companion registry. [OPUS-5] sparq-org/sparq#5235, generalising the #2384 fix. A GENERATED COMPANION is a file that is COMMITTED to git but DERIVED from other committed sources, and pinned by a byte-comparing (or regenerate-and-diff) gate. Such a pair carries a scope trap: a bead/issue/PR scoped to the SOURCE ALONE forbids the companion regeneration it simultaneously requires, so the worker must decline (#2384) or land a red gate. The fix is always the same two things, and this registry is what makes them checkable: (a) the EXACT regeneration command is recorded here and next to the source, and (b) the TWO-FILE SCOPE RULE is stated in every `scope_anchors` file — i.e. in a file the task DECOMPOSER actually reads when it scopes the source. scripts/check-generated-companions.py enforces C1 (every registered path resolves), C2 (every scope-anchor file states the rule AND names the companion path), C3 (every scripts/tests/*.golden.* file is registered here, so a new golden cannot land undeclared). Adding a checked-in generated artifact = adding an entry here. Deleting one = deleting its entry.
_marker: The literal token every scope-anchor must contain, alongside the companion path, is TWO-FILE (matched case-insensitively). Chosen to be greppable — `git grep -il two-file` finds the anchors — but that grep is a SUPERSET, not the anchor list: the phrase also occurs in this registry, in the checker, in the docs-quality wiring, and in scripts/check-fv-manifest.py, which uses it for an unrelated config relation (KANI_STEP_BUDGET vs a workflow backstop) and is NOT a generated companion. The authoritative anchor list is the `scope_anchors` of the entries below.

scripts/tests/feature-matrix-legnames.go.trigger: ONLY when the emitted leg-NAME set changes — adding, removing or renaming a leg. Editing a leg's features/test/tier/tier-reason or its comments leaves the name set untouched and stays a SINGLE-file change; do not scope the golden into a task that cannot change a `name:`.

scripts/tests/fast-fix-ring.golden.yml.trigger: ANY edit to the workflow, including a comment — the pin is the whole file and deliberately does not strip comments, so there is no single-file edit. The golden bump IS the human-review checkpoint for this security-load-bearing workflow (#3475); regenerate it in the SAME PR, never hand-edit it.

bench/dashboard/metric-labels.json.pinned_by: python3 scripts/gen-metric-labels.py --check (regenerate in memory + diff the committed file)
bench/dashboard/metric-labels.json.trigger: Adding, removing or renaming a benchmark query `.rq` file (the label map is keyed by `file_stem()`), or adding a deep-taxonomy tier. Editing a query's BODY does not move the stem and stays a SINGLE-file change.
